extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, and legal scholars interpreting early U.S. patent statutes
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts substantive legal requirements, procedural rules, and evidentiary standards from early U.S. patent statutes (Acts of 1790, 1793, and related provisions) governing who may obtain patents, what must be disclosed, fees, remedies, defenses, and administrative procedure. Useful for patent lawyers, historians, and applicants working from or comparing historical statutory rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional grant of patent power
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Congress shall have power ... to promote the progress of science and useful arts, by securing for limited times to Authors and Inventors the exclusive right to their respective writings and discoveries."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes congressional authority to create patent law and to set terms/conditions; background authority for all subsequent statutory rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal jurisdiction over patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: "The jurisdiction of the circuit courts of the United States embraces, therefore, all cases, both at law and in equity, arising under the patent laws ... this jurisdiction is exclusive, and the state courts cannot entertain a suit for the infringement of a patent, or to declare a patent void."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent infringement and related equity relief (e.g., injunctions) are to be handled in federal circuit courts; appeals to Supreme Court bring the whole case when allowed under the statute's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent grant predicate: petition and official determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are to be granted "upon the petition of any person ... setting forth, that he, she, or they, hath or have invented or discovered any useful art, manufacture, engine, machine, or device ..." and when officials "shall deem the invention or discovery sufficiently useful and important" letters patent may be made out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent requires an application/petition and positive official finding by specified officers (Secretary of State, Secretary for War, Attorney General or two of them in 1790) that the invention is useful and important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were for a term not exceeding fourteen years (e.g., "for any exceeding fourteen years, the sole and exclusive right ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory patent expiration term fixed the duration of exclusivity (14 years in these acts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification: clarity, fullness, and distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: "The specification ... shall be so particular, and said models so exact, as not only to distinguish the invention or discovery from other things before known and used, but also to enable a workman or other person skilled in the art ... to make, construct, or use the same ..." (also phrased as "clearly, truly, and fully").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires written description and enablement: the specification must distinguish the claimed invention from prior known things and enable a skilled person to practice it; certified copies are admissible evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification content for machines and compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: For machines: "he shall fully explain the principle, and the several modes in which he has contemplated the application of that principle"; for compositions: supply "specimens of the ingredients, and of the composition of matter, sufficient in quantity for the purpose of experiment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different subject-matter-specific disclosure duties: explain operating principle and modes for machines; provide sufficient specimens/quantities for compositions to permit experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models and drawings requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor shall deliver models (if the Secretary shall deem such model necessary) and drawings and written references where the nature of the case admits of drawings; models "so exact" as to enable manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, physical models or drawings must accompany the specification; Secretary may require a model; the statute also permits others to obtain permission to make similar models at their expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/affirmation of inventorship and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Every inventor, before presenting his invention, shall swear or affirm he "does verily believe, that he is the true inventor" and (for aliens) that the invention "hath not, to the best of his or her knowledge or belief, been known or used either in this or any foreign country."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An express sworn statement of being the true inventor and belief in novelty is required as a precondition to patent; false or surreptitious procurement may be challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on trivial variations as discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: "Simply changing the form or the proportions of any machine, or composition of matter, in any degree, shall not be deemed a discovery."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere changes in form/proportion (insubstantial modifications) are not patentable subject matter under these statutes — requires more than trivial variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents as prima facie evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: "In all actions for patent penalty ... the said patents or specifications shall be prima facie evidence, that the said patentee or patentees was or were the first and true inventor ... and that the same is truly specified;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A granted patent/specification carries initial evidentiary weight of inventorship and accurate disclosure but is rebuttable by the defendant with specified defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's defenses to patent enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant may plead the general issue and give the act and any special matter (with 30 days' written notice) in evidence, e.g., that "the specification filed by the plaintiff does not contain the whole of the truth ... or that it contains more than is necessary ..." and if concealment or addition was intended or actually misled the public so the described effect cannot be produced by the means specified, verdict shall be for the defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits invalidity defenses based on inadequate or deceptive specification, prior public use/description, surreptitious procurement, or claiming more than necessary; requires notice for special matters and can lead to patent being declared void and costs for defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits to challenge surreptitious or fraudulently obtained patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Under earlier act: motion may be made "within one year after issuing the said patent, but not afterwards"; later provisions allow motion "within three years after issuing the said patent, but not afterwards."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute sets explicit statutory windows (1 year in some provisions; 3 years in later provisions) for bringing an oath/affirmation-based challenge that a patent was obtained surreptitiously or by false suggestion; if successful the patent may be repealed and costs awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for repeal of a patent obtained improperly
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon oath/affirmation that patent was obtained surreptitiously or upon false suggestion, judge may grant rule and, if sufficient cause shown, order process leading to repeal; if patentee "was not the first and true inventor ... judgment shall be rendered ... for the repeal of such patent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial process allows cancellation of patents obtained by fraud/surreptitious means; unsuccessful challenger may be liable for defendant's costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and damages for infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person makes, uses, or vends a patented thing without consent, "every person so offending, shall forfeit and pay to the said patentee ... such damages as shall be assessed by a jury" and may forfeit the infringing things which may be recovered in action on the case. Some provisions prescribe at least three times the usual price or three times actual damage sustained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil remedies include damages (jury-assessed), recovery of infringing articles, and in some provisions treble damages or a multiple tied to the patentee's usual price/licensing; actions brought in circuit courts or other competent courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation and assignment of patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: "It shall be lawful for any inventor ... to record the title and interest in the said invention ... the assignee having recorded the said assignment in the office of the Secretary of State, shall thereafter stand in the place of the original inventor, both as to right and responsibility."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments of patent rights should be recorded with the governmental office; recorded assignee steps into inventor's legal position for rights and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interfering applications resolution by arbitration
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of interfering applications, "the same shall be submitted to the arbitration of three persons, one of whom shall be chosen by each of the applicants, and the third person shall be appointed by the Secretary of State; and the decision or award ... shall be final, as far as respects the granting of the patent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing claims to the same invention are resolved by a three-arbitrator panel (two chosen by parties; third by Secretary); refusal to choose an arbitrator forfeits the patent to the other party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to copies and permission to make similar models
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon application for a copy of any such specification, "it shall be the duty of the Secretary to give such copy, and to permit the person so applying for a similar model or models, to take, or make, or cause the same to be taken or made, at the expense of such applicant."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute contemplates public access to specifications and regulated ability to make similar models (at applicant's expense); certified copies are competent evidence in courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and administrative payment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified fees include: in 1790-era schemes, fees such as 50 cents for receiving/filing petition, 10 cents per 100 words for filing specifications, $2 for making out patent, $1 for affixing great seal, etc.; later provisions require inventor to pay $30 to the treasury before presenting petition and provide copying fees (20 cents per 100 words; $2 per drawing copy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must pay prescribed statutory fees at various stages (petition filing, specification copies, patent issuance); nonpayment may prevent or delay patent issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-exclusive rights and interaction with federal patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any State, before its adoption of the present form of government, shall have granted an exclusive right to any invention, "the party, claiming that right, shall not be capable of obtaining an exclusive right under this act, but on relinquishing his right under such particular State ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain a federal patent, prior state-granted exclusive rights must be relinquished; statute prevents double exclusivity absent relinquishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession on inventor's death
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor shall die before any patent is granted, "the right of applying for and obtaining such patent, shall devolve on the legal representatives of such person in trust for the heirs at law ..." and the oath/affirmation shall be varied to apply to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal representatives may pursue patent applications on behalf of deceased inventors; procedures and oaths are adaptably applied to successors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of suspended suits after repeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Suits, actions, process and proceedings formerly had under an earlier act that were set aside, suspended or abated by repeal "may be restored ... within one year from and after the passing of this act" to the same situation as before repeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional procedural rule allowing parties to revive previously suspended patent litigation within a statutory window after repeal of prior law.
